description: Generic forward / backward / stepwise variable selection driven by an information criterion (SBC/BIC), matching the structure PROC GLMSELECT uses. Forward and backward are special cases of the same stepwise loop.

sbc_definition.title: SBC (Schwarz Bayesian Criterion) for OLS = n*ln(SSE/n) + k*ln(n); lower is better.
rule: For a least-squares fit with n observations and k estimated parameters (including the intercept), SBC = n * ln(SSE / n) + k * ln(n).
An additive constant that is identical across candidate models cancels in comparisons, so only differences matter.
Lower SBC is preferred. SBC penalizes extra parameters more strongly than AIC as n grows, so it selects sparser models.
Compute SSE from the aliasing-aware fit and count k as the model RANK (non-aliased columns), not the nominal number of terms.
pitfalls: Counting nominal terms instead of rank inflates k when columns are aliased.
Mixing criteria (e.g. comparing an AIC-chosen step to an SBC baseline) will not reproduce a SBC-based SAS run.

stepwise_generalizes.title: Forward and backward selection are the two halves of one stepwise loop.
rule: One generic engine covers all three modes; only the allowed moves differ:
- FORWARD: start from the intercept (plus any forced/required variables); at each step add the single candidate whose entry most improves the criterion; stop when no addition improves it.
- BACKWARD: start from the full set of candidates; at each step remove the single variable whose removal most improves the criterion; stop when no removal improves it.
- STEPWISE: at each iteration try a forward entry, then a backward removal, so a variable added earlier can later be dropped once others enter.
Always guard candidate ENTRY with a singularity/redundancy check so an aliased column is never added (see sas_singularity_rank and class_glm_encoding).
Respect forced-in variables (they can never be removed) and keep evaluation deterministic (fixed candidate order) so ties break the same way each run.

When selection uses cross-validation with RANDOM folds (choose=cv cvmethod=random), the chosen step depends on fold assignment and is not reproducible across engines; prefer a deterministic criterion (SBC/SL) or a fixed seed for exact comparison.
pitfalls: Re-standardizing or refitting inconsistently between the entry test and the final fit changes which variable wins.
Non-deterministic candidate ordering makes tie-breaking (and therefore the whole path) irreproducible.
Removing a forced variable, or adding a redundant dummy, diverges from SAS immediately.
